findings.title: Hook file exceeds the project's ~300-line guide, and a lint rule is disabled to cope
findings.description:
The hook is about 366 lines, over the ~300-line guide in CLAUDE.md. `eslint.config.js` also turns off `react-hooks/refs` for this file. The justification comment is thorough, but it still switches off a React-correctness rule on the file that holds the most ref-heavy logic. Two things would remove the need for the suppression:
- Move the mount/teardown sequence into a plain helper module, for example `mountChart(container, style, onResize)`, returning a `{ provider, teardown }` object. That shrinks the file and keeps refs out of the facade's construction path.
- Move the long narrative comment blocks into the helper module, since much of the file's length is comments.

findings.title: The range effect does not re-run when the first series is added
findings.description: The effect that applies the visible range reads `seriesCountRef.current`. That is a ref, not state, so it is not in the dependency array. Adding the first series therefore does not apply the `range` the Context already holds. The range reaches the chart only on the next range change. The test `applies the range once a series exists` hides this by calling `setRange(NEXT_RANGE)` after `addSeries`. Initiative 120 will hit this as soon as it adds data. Either track the series count as state, or have the `addSeries` path re-apply the current range. Add a test that adds a series without changing the range afterwards.

findings.title: Subscription handlers are effectively dead code
findings.description: Both handlers have the body `if (disposedRef.current) { return }` and do nothing else. The comments say this is deliberate, to exercise the disposer lifecycle. It still adds a subscription pair, a retained-disposer array, and the teardown loop for zero behavior. That conflicts with "resist adding complexity". Defer these subscriptions until initiative 120 has a consumer, or expose them only through the facade, which already forwards them.

findings.title: Facade and error-funnel tests duplicate the same helpers across files
findings.description: `measuredRect`, `MEASURED`, and the `measure` ref callback are copied in the errors, facade, translation, and resize test files. The resize file inlines a slightly different version. `render-with-contexts.tsx` was extracted to avoid exactly this duplication, but these helpers were not. Move them into `src/test/support/` so changing the stub happens in one place.

findings.title: Type assertions and non-null assertions in tests and e2e
findings.description: The e2e spec uses `box!`, `containerBox!`, and `before!`, and the unit tests use `as DOMRect` and `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>`. The TypeScript rules call `as` a code smell and ask for a comment on each one. These are test-only, so they are low impact. Narrowing with an explicit throw or `expect(...).not.toBeNull()` would avoid the `!`. The `as` casts should carry a one-line reason.

findings.title: Mode-gated harness route and e2e build mode
findings.description: `import.meta.env.MODE === 'e2e' || … === 'development'` is deliberately written as direct comparisons so Vite can tree-shake it. The comment says the production bundle was grepped to confirm the harness is gone. Consider adding a CI check for that grep, because a future refactor to `MODES.includes(...)` would silently ship the harness. The mode strings are also scattered across `router.ts` and `playwright.config.ts`, which breaks the "define once" rule. This is acceptable here because of the tree-shaking constraint.

findings.title: Lifecycle, error funnel, and teardown design
findings.description: Mount failures are logged, surfaced as hook state, and torn down through a single path. Disposers are retained one push at a time, so a throw in the second subscription does not leak the first. Teardown order is unsubscribe, then disconnect, then destroy, then null the ref. Every catch either logs with `console.error` or carries a comment explaining why it swallows. The tests cover StrictMode double-invoke, subscribe throws, observer disconnect, and the post-teardown race.

findings.title: Stale references removed and docs updated
findings.description: `WorkspaceRoute` has no remaining references in the source. The smoke spec's "coming soon" assertion was replaced to match the new UI. `src/routes/routes.tsx`, `router.ts`, and `App.tsx` comments reflect the new behavior.
